items.title: Google has released its first decision model, Gemini Decision 1, scoring 66 on the Artificial Analys...
items.content:
Google has released its first decision model, Gemini Decision 1, scoring 66 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index and leading in knowledge and reasoning benchmarks

Gemini Decision 1 from @GoogleDeepMind scores 66 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1, in line with Elephant 9B (@baselabs) and Jev 1.14 (@typesafeai), and 7 points behind leaders Drex Max v1.1 (@NaceAI) and GLiDE v1.2 (@fastinoAI), which both score 73. It is priced at $0.10 per 1M input tokens and costs $345 per 1M Tasks across the Index, around three times higher than Drex Max v1.1 ($103) due to its higher pricing

Key results for Gemini Decision 1:

➤ Not yet frontier on Decision Index: Gemini Decision 1 scores 66 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index. It leads knowledge and reasoning benchmarks, scoring 66 on AA-Omniscience-Decision and 49 on HLE-MultiChoice. It trails on other evaluations, including our new proprietary classification and extraction benchmark AA-Paperclip, where it answers all 15 questions correctly on 33% of documents vs. 63% for Drex Max v1.1

➤ More than 3x the Cost per Task of leading models: Gemini Decision 1 costs $345 per 1M Tasks, compared with $103 for Drex Max v1.1, $156 for Jev 1.14. This difference is driven by its token price of $0.10 per 1M input tokens vs. $0.03 for Drex Max v1.1. Gemini Decision 1 has a similar Cost per 1M Tasks to GPT-6 Luna (Decisions, $339)

➤ Strong calibration for reasoning tasks: We measure calibration with the Brier score, the average squared gap between the probability a model assigns to its chosen answer and whether that answer was correct (lower is better). Gemini Decision 1 has a Brier score of 0.18 across the Index, between Drex Max v1.1 (0.16) and Jev 1.14 (0.19). Calibration varies by task. with its Brier score of 0.20 on HLE-MultiChoice among the lowest of all models in the Index, while its 0.14 on When2Call compares with 0.04 for Drex Max v1.1

1. CTF red-teaming should prompt explicitl...
items.content:
New research on red teaming our sandbox platform SPACE: 

1. CTF red-teaming should prompt explicitly to break the host-guest isolation. 

2. Non-cyber models are actually better than cyber models at red teaming and finding exploits (eg GPT 5.6 Sol vs GPT 5.6 Sol Cyber)

3. Our sandbox platform SPACE was robust to sandbox isolation exploits 

4. Network bypassing with DNS spoofing was something we discovered and addressed 

5. Our platform is open-source and we want to keep sharing our findings openly for the agent sandbox and security community.

items.title: Former White House AI advisor @BuchananBen says China could already be ahead of the US in AI if Wash...
items.content:
Former White House AI advisor @BuchananBen says China could already be ahead of the US in AI if Washington hadn't restricted its access to advanced NVIDIA chips:

"If we were selling China as many chips as they could buy, they'd buy a lot of chips, and they would be, if not ahead, much, much, much closer."

"China does not lack for electricity. They certainly don't lack for talent. We read the DeepSeek papers while we were in the White House. The one thing China lacks is chips."

"If you look at the comments of the leading Chinese AI CEOs, the DeepSeek CEO being just one of them, they all universally agree that they don't lack for money, they don't lack for talent, they lack for computing power."

"If President Trump had enforced the export controls better, I think we'd be ahead by even more. He repealed a lot of this and has declined to enforce other parts of it."

"It is a policy choice to let the Chinese be even as close as they are."

items.title:
End of an era. 

Was just watching the video that I shot of Jensen at GTC this spring. He was on top...
items.content:
End of an era. 

Was just watching the video that I shot of Jensen at GTC this spring. He was on top of the world. Had built one of America's best companies. Was talking to a hockey stadium with every seat filled. Took hours to talk with the press, answering every question. 

Now not just his personal life, but his business life is on fire. The WSJ and NYT are saying the board is meeting right now to fire him. 

One thing I learned at Microsoft is to keep your head when everything is going wrong. And this series of affairs has cost me some money, and probably will tomorrow. As it will many of you who are investors in NVIDIA.

One thing about NVIDIA. It has a very strong bench of people who could run the company. You don't know that because Jensen was the only one who built a relationship with the market. He is so strongly tied to the company. 

Let's be honest. It's a huge loss for NVIDIA. Last week no one had any questions about the governance of the company. Now the knives are out and blood will flow in the board room. 

But NVIDIA will survive. It will see a better day again. 

Here's my expectations. That tomorrow two new committees will be announced:

1. An executive search committee.
2. A temporary executive committee.

Knowing NVIDIA from a close seat. I'm very confident that it will continue doing well after this all gets cleaned up. The talent bench there is so deep. 

I'm not selling my stock.

items.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: UK chip startup Fractile just raised $720M, and its valuation jumped from about...
items.content:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: UK chip startup Fractile just raised $720M, and its valuation jumped from about $1B to $7B in 6 months.

• Fractile was founded in 2022 by Walter Goodwin, a roboticist from the University of Oxford
• Its chips stack memory right on top of the processor instead of using the high-bandwidth memory most AI chips rely on
• The $6.5B figure is pre-money, so Fractile is worth about $7B with the new cash, making it one of Britain's most valuable tech startups
• The reported Anthropic deal covers roughly $250M of chips that won't be ready until 2027, and Fractile hopes to expand it
• Returning backers Accel, Conviction and Felicis joined new investors like Balderton and T. Rowe Price

@sophiadew: "This is a larger signal about how the UK is seeing sovereign AI hardware evolve, what their priorities are."

items.title: Take away its tools, and Claude Fable 5.2 scores below Claude Haiku 5.5 with tools on VIALS-AA; acro...
items.content:
Take away its tools, and Claude Fable 5.2 scores below Claude Haiku 5.5 with tools on VIALS-AA; across models tool use nearly doubles scores, from ~25% to ~47% on average

VIALS-AA is our implementation of @joinHandshakeAI's VIALS benchmark for visual reasoning in life sciences research. By default, models work as agents: they think, run code and view images in a sandbox. We reran VIALS-AA in a one-shot format: one request with the question and images, and no tools.

Lower cost models in an agent harness can beat single-shot large models on both cost and performance in visual reasoning and interpretation of scientific artifacts.

Claude Fable 5.2 (max) leads VIALS-AA at 67% with tools, at a cost of $4.20 per task; without tools it scores 44% at $0.73 per task. Claude Haiku 5.5 (max) scores 49% with tools, at $0.07 per task: higher than Fable without tools, at about a tenth of the cost.

items.title: Former White House AI advisor @BuchananBen admits the Biden administration should have moved 30-50% ...
items.content:
Former White House AI advisor @BuchananBen admits the Biden administration should have moved 30-50% more aggressively on AI, revealing how Washington underestimated memory chips and failed to stop chip smuggling:

"We probably would've done them 30 to 50% more aggressively, and we would have done them sooner. The federal government is a very big battleship."

"The first memo on the chip controls was in 2021. The chip control didn't happen till October 2022."

"We didn't recognize in 2022 that we would see a shift to test time compute that made memory chips even more important."

"There was smuggling of chips and chip dies that the Department of Commerce did not stop. That was a failure of the US government to fully implement the policy."

items.content:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: Runway just released Praxis-1 with open weights, a robot model trained mostly on regular video instead of robot data.

• Runway, best known for AI video, first showed Praxis-1 in September and tested it with early partners before opening it up
• Its bet is that robot demonstration data is scarce, but video is "effectively limitless"
• In Runway's tests, pretraining on web video worked about as well as pretraining on real robot footage, with 16.1 cm vs 16.0 cm of placement error
• The same policy ran in a studio and a home kitchen without retraining
• Runway's benchmark results, it beats Black Forest Labs' FLUX 3 Action, NVIDIA’s Cosmos 3 Nano and Physical Intelligence’s π0.5

@sophiadew: "There's some really cool robots that are actually being built with the Praxis-1."

items.title: We are publishing new research on our findings from red-teaming SPACE, our VM sandbox for Computer a...
items.content:
We are publishing new research on our findings from red-teaming SPACE, our VM sandbox for Computer agents.

We gave 12 models two tasks: escape the VM to take a credential from the host, and bypass SPACE's network policy to reach a blocked URL.

We found that the standard Capture the Flag setup used in red-teaming can steer agents away from the security boundary being tested, and that security-specialized models don't guarantee better results.

https://t.co/Egh3x3uX4c

items.title: IBM GM Shaun Clowes says even Claude Code is still just a copilot, fundamentally limited by human sp...
items.content:
IBM GM Shaun Clowes says even Claude Code is still just a copilot, fundamentally limited by human speed.

The real AI breakthrough will come when entire business functions operate autonomously, without human oversight:

"We started with chatbots, which are effectively a way to learn together, a way to explore a problem space together, humans and machines."

"Then we move towards copilots, which I would even describe tools like Claude Code are still copilots because they're a human working together with an agent to build something. But they’re still fundamentally limited by the speed of humans."

"The goal isn't just for builders building things to be accelerated with AI, it's for every business process you can imagine to be accelerated."

"We will know when we're really getting there when we start to see whole sections of businesses get automated with no human oversight. I think we’re just at the very tip of that."
@confluentinc @IBM

Today, @llama_index is an applied research lab for document OCR and document work.

Our core focus i...
items.content:
Today, @llama_index is an applied research lab for document OCR and document work.

Our core focus is investing in building the best-in-class models+ agents at the pareto frontier of accuracy/cost/latency for document processing. 

To do this, we have to invest in all the different components around the research infra stack: 
1. Building comprehensive and fair benchmarks. Today we have ParseBench, ExtractBench, and ExtractBench Pro. They're already the most popular benchmarks in parsing and extraction today, and we're just getting started.
2. Investing in data curation and synthetic data generation. 
3. Investing in compute and our training pipeline. This has produced models like OCRia-1. 
4. Investing in agent optimization - tune everything around the models to further hillclimb cost and accuracy.
5. Closing the loop based on feedback - whether from active usage of our product, implicit/explicit customer feedback, or automated verification. 

We are accelerating our capabilities at a crazy pace. Today, our work is documented in our research page: https://t.co/ojqNkpZAvu

There is a lot more to come!

items.title: Tools matter most for counting tasks, which need an exact tally of many small objects. With tools, m...
items.content:
Tools matter most for counting tasks, which need an exact tally of many small objects. With tools, models can crop, pull pixel-level intensities and further manipulate images to separate objects and count them in code. Without them, they have to estimate from what they see.

On the 23 cell counting and quantification tasks in VIALS-AA, Fable drops from a 65% pass^3 rate with tools to just 9% without. Claude Opus 5.5 (max) falls from 57% to 4%, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) falls from 65% to 13%.

GPT-6 Astra (max) and GPT-6.1 Sol (max) hold up better: Astra passes 61% with tools and 35% without, and Sol falls from 61% to 39%. Some domains depend less on tools: on the 23 phylogenetics tasks, Astra passes 78% with tools and 83% without.

items.content:
Rox CEO @ishanmkh says the era of selling AI agents on "hours saved" is dead, after years of Microsoft Copilot and Agentforce failing to move the needle for enterprise buyers:

"Deploying AI and agents where you're measuring the success by hours saved per employee per week, that is dead. That is done."

"They've been buying Microsoft Copilot, and then Agentforce, and all of these archaic agent systems for about three years now, and all of those were sold on the value proposition of saving time. So the buyers are fatigued. It never really moved the needle."

"What people want now is coding agents that can ship code, and they want revenue agents that can ship revenue. You can either help save money or make money, or avoid existential risk, like with cybersecurity."

"Saving some time for employees is just the wrong goal."
@rox_ai

items.content:
We think the most scalable source of robotics data is general video. A model trained to predict that video learns how objects behave, how hands move and what a task looks like partway through, giving it a head start on new embodiments.

items.content:
Here is a big problem with agentic coding:

The more code you write, the more complex it is to keep the application from blowing up in users' faces.

For every new feature you implement:

• You need to determine how to measure it
• You need to plan who gets it first
• You need to decide when to let more people use it
• You need a rollback strategy for when things go wrong

This is a huge problem, but we can fix this very easily! ↓

items.title: Tools raise the cost per task for every model, but by very different amounts. Astra costs $0.27 per ...
items.content:
Tools raise the cost per task for every model, but by very different amounts. Astra costs $0.27 per task with tools and $0.21 without, and Sol $0.06 and $0.05. Fable costs $4.20 with tools and $0.73 without, a 5.8× difference. The largest multiples are Qwen3.8 Max (0902, xhigh) at 28×, Gemini 3.8 Flash at 20× and MiMo-V2.6-Pro at 15×.

The cheapest way to reach a given score is often a smaller model with tools. Haiku with tools scores 49% at $0.07 per task, while Opus without tools scores 34% at $0.33.

Runway Co-CEO @agermanidis explains why AI video models could become the brains of physical robots:
...
items.content:
Runway Co-CEO @agermanidis explains why AI video models could become the brains of physical robots:

By learning to predict video, they're also learning physics, human behavior, and how the real world works.

"What are you essentially doing when you're training a model to predict pixels and predict video?"

"You're learning about how the world works. You're learning about physics. You learn about how do humans perform different tasks out in the world, how they play sports, perform household tasks."

"If a model becomes really good at predicting video, predicting all those observations from the world, then there is no reason it should not be able to predict the same thing but in an action format that's compatible with something that you would use to control a robot."

"The main thesis of Runway is if you train models that are good enough at simulating the world, then they're gonna be useful obviously for media and content creation and marketing and advertising, but they're also gonna be useful for any kind of system that interacts with the physical world."
@runwayml

items.title:
ADM 3 Cloud edits a photo better than it makes one from scratch

ADM 3 Cloud is Apple's new image mo...
items.content:
ADM 3 Cloud edits a photo better than it makes one from scratch

ADM 3 Cloud is Apple's new image model on Private Cloud Compute. It shipped with iOS 27 on September 14 and powers the photo editing tools in Photos, like Spatial Reframing, plus Image Playground and Genmoji.

In our testing, it's strongest at swapping and changing things in a photo. Clean-ups and fixes land a little below its overall rank, and reframing a shot is its weak spot. Making images from scratch is weaker again.

It's available through Apple Intelligence on iPhone 15 Pro and later, and on M1 or later iPads and Macs, with daily usage limits.

With no API, we tested it through a Mac app we built on Image Playground. Apple refused 8% of our prompts. We evaluated it on only the images it returned.

items.content:
The largest gains from tools go mostly to models that score lowest without them. The ten models that score below 31% without tools average ~42 tool calls per task, while the seven above average ~23.

MiMo-V2.6-Pro shows the largest gain of any model: it scores 5% without tools and 43% with them, making ~49 tool calls per task. Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) makes ~68 tool calls per task and moves from 16% to 41%.

Astra and Sol make the fewest tool calls of any model, ~8 per task, and gain 13 and 16 points, respectively.

items.title: I'm seeing hundreds of posts about Fable 5.2. Usually don't like sharing video games, but it is such...
items.content:
I'm seeing hundreds of posts about Fable 5.2. Usually don't like sharing video games, but it is such a strong trend worth to talk about this for a bit.

Making a game (or really anything, a song, an app, a movie) isn't the gating factor. A few hundred bucks, some creativity, and a weekend and you can get something compelling built.

But here on X the AI community alone generates about 30,000 posts a day. 

Distribution and attention are the gating factors and that's getting tougher and tougher over time. 

In a sea of video games, how does your video game get anyone to try it? 

I was just talking with another entrepreneur who is building a virtual being company. I gave him a lot of heck because he had the same problem. His virtual being isn't as good as @nuance_ai or @tavus and didn't have a good answer for how he'd get his virtual being to do something those two can't. 

It's one thing to make a cute song to send to grandma to get her to laugh. It's a whole other thing to build a catalog, a brand, and something that really makes them stand out. 

Taste, the AI people in SF say. 

But it is more than that. It's having something that yours does that the others don't have yet that makes it at least stand out on X. If you hit that mark you'll get reach, since there's thousands of influencers looking for cool stuff to push.

But even getting a viral post isn't enough to get anyone to care for more than an hour. 

This is the downside of building that a lot of VCs/investors aren't really being honest with entrepreneurs about. 

It's a great time to build a business, since building has gotten a lot cheaper than it used to be, but now that it's a lot cheaper there is a lot more to consider (I just passed 10,000 companies on my AI lists here on X at https://t.co/9eRY65x3IQ which underscores my point). 

Competition is brutal all of a sudden. Everyone sees the big money going to a bunch of companies and one thing they did is to stand out over and over and bring something to the table that the others aren't. 

That said, everyone has different motivations for building and not everything has to lead to a company, which I get. 

Just something I'm seeing when I talk with entrepreneurs and watch what they are doing.

There wasn't much technology to work with in terms of interior design with my app 🏡 Interior AI the last 12 months

For 4 years it's been based on simple image models: photos of your interior as input -> redesigns out as output

But now there is a completely new dimension to it 😬

As you probably saw on your timeline, AI can finally generate headless Blender 3d scenes from just a rough video (which I did today of my living room), or even a few photos, and even a floorplan (which no image model was able to understand before, believe me I tried 100 times!)

That means that 3d scene I can then make fully editable in my app Interior AI

Meaning you can paint any wall, floor or ceiling any color, next move around, delete or add new furniture etc from a giant 3d library of furniture

Endless possibilities!!

I think I found my next big feature 😍

I'll try get something live in Interior AI within the next few hours!!!

items.content:
The idea is straightforward: Use agents to help you prepare and manage every release.

Here is how Release Autopilot from @LaunchDarkly works:

1. You define a release policy with the rules for how you want any new changes on your system to reach your users.

2. The Release Autopilot agents will examine every code change, determine its risk, and recommend whether it needs a feature flag. A flag is a switch that lets you control who gets the new behavior.

3. Release Autopilot also sets up success metrics for the change and prepares a release plan.

4. You review the proposal in GitHub, request changes, reject it, or approve it through PR comments.

5. After you approve and merge the changes, the release starts with a small group of users.

6. LaunchDarkly monitors how that specific change performs in production, and it automatically expands access as long as everything works.

7. If there are any regressions, the platform will automatically turn off the problematic feature, so you have time to check what went wrong and fix it.

Here is more information about how Release Autopilot works: https://t.co/SUQOut6nID

Thanks to the @LaunchDarkly team for partnering with me on this post.

ElevenLabs Field CTO @i_am_holt explains why voice AI is harder than text:

An agent can give the ex...
items.content:
ElevenLabs Field CTO @i_am_holt explains why voice AI is harder than text:

An agent can give the exact same answer and either reassure or frustrate a customer, depending entirely on its tone.

"Everything that makes AI agents hard is also something that makes a voice agent hard. It doesn't recommend you go to a competitor, it doesn't give a refund when it’s not supposed to."

"It's harder to understand voice than it is text. Different accents, different dialects, different languages. And when you're speaking back to a user, delivery is so much more important."

"You can say the same sentence in 100 different ways and have different meaning depending on how you say the words."

"Saying you can't have a refund, there are two very different ways that that can be interpreted. In both cases you're saying the same thing, but whether or not you sound empathetic is actually the difference between success and failure."
@ElevenLabs

"Saying you can't have a refund, there are two very different ways that that can be interpreted. In both cases you're saying the same thing, but whether or not you sound empathetic is actually the difference between success and failure."

@ElevenLabs

items.title: Humble Robotics CEO @engineered predicts autonomous vehicles will be everywhere within the next deca...
items.content:
Humble Robotics CEO @engineered predicts autonomous vehicles will be everywhere within the next decade, as AI replaces hand-coded driving systems with models that learn the world:

"Waymo showed that robotaxis were possible, and they've had a great safety record and I take them all the time in San Francisco, and they're expanding and they're scaling, right?"

"So right away people started going like, 'Wait a minute. If that's possible, what else is possible.'"

"10 years ago when I started working on this, just about everything that we were doing was kind of like this hand-coded like let me look at this image, and let me see where the lane lines are, let me like count the pixels of the lanes."

"And you don't do any of that anymore. It's like you have a model, it learns the world, it drives."

"In 10 years, it's just gonna be, I think, AVs literally everywhere applied to just about every vehicle."
@humblerobotics

items.title:
Benford’s Law: https://t.co/OjP2EEtxUo

Fraud detection is just one of its many practical powerful a...
items.content:
Benford’s Law: https://t.co/OjP2EEtxUo

Fraud detection is just one of its many practical powerful applications!

Amazon Summary:

“This book provides the first comprehensive treatment of Benford's law, the surprising logarithmic distribution of significant digits discovered in the late nineteenth century. Establishing the mathematical and statistical principles that underpin this intriguing phenomenon, the text combines up-to-date theoretical results with overviews of the law’s colorful history, rapidly growing body of empirical evidence, and wide range of applications.

An Introduction to Benford’s Law begins with basic facts about significant digits, Benford functions, sequences, and random variables, including tools from the theory of uniform distribution. After introducing the scale-, base-, and sum-invariance characterizations of the law, the book develops the significant-digit properties of both deterministic and stochastic processes, such as iterations of functions, powers of matrices, differential equations, and products, powers, and mixtures of random variables. Two concluding chapters survey the finitely additive theory and the flourishing applications of Benford’s law.

Carefully selected diagrams, tables, and close to 150 examples illuminate the main concepts throughout. The text includes many open problems, in addition to dozens of new basic theorems and all the main references. A distinguishing feature is the emphasis on the surprising ubiquity and robustness of the significant-digit law. This text can serve as both a primary reference and a basis for seminars and courses.”

🇺🇸 The Eleventh Hour, The Eleventh Day, The Eleventh Month — Veterans Day 2026: Honoring America’s Warriors!

November 11, 1918 — 11:00 AM!

The guns of World War I fell silent on the Western Front. After many years of devastating warfare, the armistice marked the end of fighting.

1938: Armistice Day became a federal holiday.

1954: President Dwight D. Eisenhower established Veterans Day to honor America's veterans of all wars.

2026: As America commemorates its 250th anniversary, we recognize generations of courage, duty, sacrifice, and military service.

From the trenches of World War I to World War II, Korea, Vietnam, Iraq, and Afghanistan, American service members have answered the nation's call.

War is not measured merely by victories but by lives sacrificed, families forever changed, and the peace that follows.
